newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on Telkom profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on Telkom profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking in heavyweight Telkom and other significant listings dragged down the Jakarta stock index at the close on Tuesday, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 5.65 points, or 0.91 percent, to close at 615.21 points after touching an earlier intra-day low of 613.38 points. Losers led gainers by 61 to 51, with 55 counters unchanged.

"Today's correction was normal after the market rallied several days ago and it has the potential to be rebound on Wednesday if Telkom's price also reverses as sentiment towards several medium-sized stocks remains firm," a foreign broker said.
An analyst from another foreign brokerage said some fund managers seemed to be watching the Jakarta bourse and re-evaluating their positions.
"Some counters have good fundamentals and offer very good long-term opportunities for investors," an analyst said.
Telecommunications firms Telkom and Indosat, cement maker Semen Gresik and cigarette maker Sampoerna were among the targets of profit-taking, brokers said.
Telkom fell 125 rupiah to 4,000 rupiah on a volume of 11.1 million shares while Indosat fell 100 rupiah to 6,900 rupiah on a volume of 1.1 million shares.
Brokers said President's Suharto call for a 15 percent ceiling for shareholders in publicly listed firms did not have much impact on the market as its remained only a suggestion.
"It is a positive sign from government but its still a long way to go before Indonesia to implements it," a foreign analyst said.
On Tuesday, an Indonesian minister quoted Suharto as saying that for the sake of equity, individual shareholdings should not exceed 15 percent in companies listed on the country's stock exchanges.
Brokers said active buying of some medium and small-sized stocks stopped the index from falling sharply.
They said, Miwon Indonesia, Mulia Industri, Daya Guna Samudera, Voksel Electric and Citra Marga were among the active stocks on fresh buying.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia topped the active list with about 15 million shares traded, rising 325 rupiah to 3,450 rupiah on its good fundamentals, brokers said.
They said positive sentiment towards the stock was also boosted by its recent acquisition of a printing company and there was market talk of a possible private placement.
A Miwon official declined to comment on issue of the private placement.
Newly-listed fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudera was actively traded with 6.5 million shares changing hands.
It rose 125 rupiah to 2,525 rupiah on what brokers said was talk of a possible better-than-expected nine-month result ahead its formal announcement.
Telecommunications cable maker Voksel Electric rose 100 rupiah to 900 rupiah on a volume of 2.1 million shares on speculation of merger. Company officials were not available for comment.
